title: Home or local fieldwork guide and risk assessment
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 25 (Home or local fieldwork guide and risk assessment (portal printable; adult supervision, no entering water))
intro: Lesson 25: Revision: physical fieldwork enquiry design and data collection (Paper 1, Section B). A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To understand how to plan a physical fieldwork enquiry and collect reliable primary and secondary data
equipment: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Geography 4GE1 specification, Paper 1 Section B (physical fieldwork)
safety: An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands

questions.q: Big question: what makes a fieldwork enquiry trustworthy?
questions.a: A clear hypothesis, suitable sampling, accurate and repeated measurements, safe methods and more than one data source

questions.q: Core: Exam-style Section B questions on the portal: justify a sampling method, describe a technique, explain one risk and how it was reduced, suggest one secondary source.
questions.a: Indicative mark points in the portal key
questions.model: Teacher does the first 3-marker: 'Justify your sampling method': name it (systematic, every 50 m), how it worked, and why it suited the aim (even coverage of the river's length).

questions.q: Extend: Explain how one technique could give unreliable data and how to improve it.
questions.a: For example: float method affected by wind (1); repeat three times and use the mean (1); use a flow meter (1)
